A skyscraper is a tall, continuously habitable building having multiple floors. Modern sources currently define skyscrapers as being at least 100 metres or 150 metres in height, though there is no universally accepted definition.

[{"score": 1, "comment": "I bought this for my driving simulator city I am building - Los Injurus City for the simulator Beamng Drive.  I have a very spartan budget so this fit the bill - but I actually bought this because it not only was a good price but I really liked the look of it.  The scale is correct and it comes with things grouped into convenient sections so you can easily wrangle the not-too-bad UV's into what you need.  My needs require super-low draw-calls since our game-engine has DirectX 11 as a fall-back if Vulkan isn't supported, so I did spend a day or more wrangling UV's sewing everything up and duplicating orphan UV's with like-textures - thank-goodness for having paid for some scripts to speed that up.
That said, the way the UV's were laid out - despite not being sewn - makes things very easy to work with.  In all honesty I have seen much, much worse.
I had to make a few small adjustments to the model, just minor nit-picks as we say here, and add doors since you'll be seeing most of it from street level -  but I have those already so it's all good.  I will add an elevator shaft shortly also, but for most this building should be fine as-is unless you're running this on a direct-x 11 or older rendering engine.
Didn't find errors with this model, and did not find 'hidden' surfaces either.  Building is easy to manipulate again due to previously mentioned groups.
If you want this for a city scene outside of video games - this is GREAT - if you are going to run this in a game, be prepared to optimize it some.  I cannot even begin to complain for the price, however, and am very satisfied.  The two smaller low-rise structures can be moved independently and arranged as satellite buildings regardless if you wish to physically have them connected with the main structure or not.  That's a nice bonus.

description_text: Hello Everyone!Today I have made a model of a skyscraper that was inspired by the design of the PetroBangla Building in Bangladesh.This model will save you a lot of time if you are making a open world video-game!This model is great for just about anything from city renderings to video games and etc.I have made this using Blender 2.9 .The HDRI that I have used to render the building was provided by HDRI Haven. https://hdrihaven.com/I have included this model in various file formats including a .blend file for you to edit the model to your preferences.In the .blend file, I have assigned different parts of the building to different materials, so it is easier for you to customize the look and color of the building.This model has 31,659 vertices, 26,199 faces and 53,423 triangles.

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 The present building was built between 1747 and 1751 with 3 ships with cane ceiling. Seven brick columns on each side separated the nave of the laterales.Entre 1832 and 1834 there were the first changes extending the ship and building the present facade in Italian neoclassical style, with two towers covered with majolica domes, designed by Catalan architect Juan Roque. In 1834 he acquired the rank of Metropolitan Cathedral. In 1940 there was another important change, changing the ceiling of the nave by one barrel vault. Inside the most interesting work is a bas-relief of Christ in marble by Pigalle, flattered by Juan Manuel de Rosas to Estanislao Lopez.

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 The first vicar was Friar Anthony of Padua Teixeira, who prayed the first mass on a provisional chapel, used while building the Matrix, inaugurated on March 25, 1781. In it was buried the founder of Campinas, Francisco Barreto Leme, on April 13 1782. The Bento Quirino Square, with its headquarters, was the "Celulla Mater" around which was formed and developed Campinas, then a drovers crossing point that went towards Goiás. In 1807 it was decided to transfer the headquarters of the parish to another place, building up a new church, the current Cathedral of Our Lady. da Conceição, which was completed and opened in 1883. It was the "Young Mother". But the people did not accept the "Old Mother" stopped being parish. Thus they claimed to continue as a parish, which was accepted by the Bishop of São Paulo, which created then the "Old Mother Church", the Parish of Santa Cruz, on May 08, 1870. In 1938, the parish was made official as N . Sra. do Carmo. The Carmo Matrix was reformed several times, and in 1929 was demolished and completely rebuilt in its neo-Gothic style it has today. On 6 November 1974, the Carmelite Mother of Pope Paul VI received the title of Basilica. The installation of the Basilica took place on June 22 the Holy Year 1975. It is a very dear church by the people of Campinas is the "Old Mother Church", the first church in the city.

description_text: The OBERLÄNDER is a basic type of the Middle Rhine ship, which of 15th up to 18th century was used mainly on the distance between Mainz and Cologne. Its shape is adapted to the particular circumstances of the current path and its fairway. The floor plan has the shape of a trapezoid. The greatest width is in the ship's bottom, and in the rear , the width of the 1.5 to 2 times the width of the bow. The floor is completely flat and is pulled up in the stern to a huge hut, which is pointed at a height of 6-7 m and steep drops to the deck. The deck has from bow to stern the same width and is completely flat. It falls against the bow. It gives the impression of heaviness, but this is not true. Top and bottom form an angle of up to 10 degrees. The 6-7 m high mast pole is used exclusively for towing. The viability of the Oberlander likely 100 - 120 t have not been exceeded. The round window is flush with the top strake, so that no transition board is available. The form shall bear halfway up two gangways, which served as the site of the Boating Party. The sites of Oberlander  were mainly in Bonn Beuel , to a lesser extent in Mainz on the Vilzbacher shipyard. Often the ships were used one or two times, than demolished to gain the wood for house construction.

overview:
Lowpoly Edwardian style townhouse with basic features; good for use as background architecture or for lowpoly game design. Optional basement level (can be easily hidden). Textures include Colour and Bump, UVs unwrapped.
History
This structure is representitive of much middle-class housing found throughout Britain and her territories at around the turn of the 20th Century. This model specifically represents a simplistic, though accurate, attempt to replicate a specific building; Laurel Villa which was in found in Kent, England until the mid 1960s when it was demolished.

description_text:
After the release of several prototypes, the Muegyetemi Sportrepulo Egyesulet (MSrE) in 1938 began the construction of the first production aircraft based on the M-19, designated M-24. The main designers of the project were Josef Szegedy and Endre Jancsó.
The aircraft was a double low wing with an elliptical wing, equipped with a German engine Hirth HM 504A-2 with a capacity of 100 hp. (75 kW).
After a successful prototype test, a small series of 5 aircraft was ordered. The first two cars in this series were sold by the Royal Air Force of Egypt.
In 1940, a modification of the aircraft was released, which received the designation M-25 Nebulo. It was also built in a small series in triplicate.
In the same year, the EMESE experimental plant was erected, where they began to build prototypes developed at MSrE. In 1942, another modification of the M-24 was completed, which received the designation M-29. And a year later, the M-27 was built at the plant, which was a training modification for fighter pilots with the German Argus As 10 engine. These prototypes did not receive further development, since the plant was destroyed as a result of the Allied bombing.

description_text:
Brazier, fired with coke or coal
Often used for waste incineration or outdoor heating during severe winters.The size of this brazier is adapted to the original dimensions, 80 cm high, 50 cm inside diameter, 60 cm outside diameter.Additionally, textures for the normal, rough, bump layers are added to the object.
Feel free to download, I sell objects at a minimum price to be able to pay the costs associated with their listing.I also invite people who would like to create an object according to their needs to contact me.
The textures mostly at the resolution of 2048 x 2048
Some objects are packed in a zip, because they have the texture catalog structure preserved together with the object, which should facilitate working with the finished model.
The files are sometimes repeated because their versions were created using different methods, e.g. fbxs are created by exporting from the source program and to it separately basic textures, and the fbx version with built-in full PBR texturing built with the object.
Feel free to download, I sell objects at a minimum price to be able to pay the costs associated with their listing.I also invite people who would like to create an object according to their needs to contact me.

description_text:
Hello,Im representing you pack of historical clay pots.It contains 5 unique static meshes.
Models were made in Blender 2.8 and they are made from quads only for better game render.Textures are 1K resolution. Pivots set on bottom of objects.Models are available in following formats

  - Blend

  - Uasset

  - Fbx

  - Obj

  - Dae

  - Ply

  - Stl

  - abc

I use Unreal Engine 4 naming convention

  - SM – static mesh (SM_Hammer)

  - M – material (M_Wood)

  - T – texture (T_Metal)

Models are game ready, you can just drag fbx to content window in UE4 and it will create and assign materials (just click import all when importing).I am a fresh 3D artist so write to me if something is wrong.

description_text: The Dauytuly Shyngysbai kazhy mosque or the Zhami mosque is the spiritual heritage of the city and one of its oldest fundamental buildings, built in the middle of the 19th century. It is located in the old part of Shymkent city. In the first half of the twentieth century, from the time of the formation of Soviet power and until the end of World War II, the building of the mosque was used as a military barracks. In 1947, the mosque was handed over for the use of the people and was named Koshkar ata. From 1947 to 1997, the mosque was considered the central regional one. In 2000, the old name Koshkar Ata was changed to the modern one. The total area of ​​the mosque is 717.3 square meters. There are two minarets in the courtyard of the mosque, the height of which is 4.8 meters and 10 meters.

description_text:
Low-poly stylized stone obelisk model made in 3ds Max, sculpted in Blender, baked and textured in Substance Painter.
Model details: 

  - Model has 2853 polygons and 2850 vertices

  - Textures come in 2k resolution

  - Texture pack contains .png, .jpeg and .targa files for UE4 and png files for vray, corona, arnold and unity_hd_render_pipeline

  - Model pack includes .fbx, .max, .blend and .obj files

  - Model scale might be pretty small - it has to be rescaled in scene or game engine

  - Textures are not included into .fbx file and have to be plugged in manually

  - Everything is placed to 0.0.0 scene coordinates

  - Everything is named properly, all elements share same UV set

  - Nothing is overlapping, nothing is animated

As usual - best wishes and have a nice day!:D

description_text:
The history of Bukhara stretches back for millennia. The origin of its inhabitants goes back to the period of Aryan immigration into the region.[1] The city itself, currently the capital of the Bukhara Province (viloyat) of Uzbekistan, is about two and a half thousand years old. Located on the Silk Road, the city has long been a centre of trade, scholarship, culture, and religion. During the Golden age of Islam, under the rule of Samanids, Bukhara became the intellectual centre of the Islamic world. In medieval times, Bukhara served as the capital of the Khanate of Bukhara and was the birthplace of Imam Bukhari.
UNESCO has listed the historic centre of Bukhara, which contains numerous mosques and madrassas, as one of the World Heritage Sites.
Bukhara functioned as one of the main centres of Persian civilization from its early days in the 6th century BCE. The city's architectural and archaeological sites form one of the pillars of Central Asian history and art.[citation needed] The region of Bukhara long formed part of the Persian Empire.

description_text: This is an 1899 Mosley Folding bathtub ad. Mosley folding bathtubs where manufactured from 1880 to 1900 as a way to bathe without having all the space needed for a traditional bathtub. They were advertised as A perfectly equipped bath and No Bathroom required. The mosley folding bathtub produced 20 styles of bathtubs over the years. The one in this pictureis a type that looked like a stand-alone mirror when closed. I have a model of another mosley ad in my store that depicts a version that was similar except the mirror did not go down to the bottom and the unused space was taken up by fake decorative drawers. If you enjoy these models please give them a like, a good review, and visit my store where I have many similar models for sale. If you have any questions about this asset, or about anything in my store, please contact me. If you have any issues please do the same before leaving a bad review, because it may be a simple mistake that I can try to fix.

description_text: In Japan, a tōrō is a traditional lantern made of stone, wood, or metal. Like many other elements of Japanese traditional architecture, it originated in China where they can still be found in Buddhist temples and Chinese gardens. They are not as common in Korea as they are in China or Japan. In Japan, tōrō were originally used only in Buddhist temples, where they lined and illuminated paths. Lit lanterns were then considered an offering to Buddha. Their use in Shinto shrines and also private homes started during the Heian period (794–1185).

description_text:
This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This is a modular tree house. It can be delievered on huge trucks as a payload and will just be hung up to a strong tree by a crane. Nine steel wires will hold it than.  This example is fixed to an european breech (fagus sylvatica) which has an maximum hight of 45m. Electric power is supplied by PV panels, hot water by solar energy. Waste water is filtered and will be used to water the tree.
this model was made for the Sketchup 3D challenge %232211. Please enjoy and rate!

description_text:
This is an industrial brick building.The model is perfect to use in the background of big scenes or inside of games as it is low-poly, but you can also use it for close-up shots.The building alone has around 2500 vertices and combining it with the rooftop decoration (which doesn't have to be used in your scene of course), the whole scene has around 56000 vertices.
You can easily change any window by shifting the texture around the model and you can place any light source in any of the rooms with windows. I chose to place the lights as they are seen in the preview images.
Note that this is only two sides of the building. You can easily expand it into having four sides but for most renders it isn't necessary and therefore saves vertices.
Downloading the .blend-file is recommended as the materials and textures will be perfectly projected onto the model other than using the .fbx- or the .obj-version.

description_text:
Concrete Barriers 
A Jersey barrier, Jersey wall, or Jersey bump is a modular concrete or plastic barrier employed to separate lanes of traffic. It is designed to minimize vehicle damage in cases of incidental contact while still preventing vehicle crossovers resulting in a likely head-on collision. Jersey barriers are also used to reroute traffic and protect pedestrians and workers during highway construction. They are named after the U.S. state of New Jersey which first started using the barriers as separators between lanes of a highway in the 1950s.

description_text:
This 3D model depicts a scene of an abandoned warehouse filled with various forgotten objects, creating a characteristic sense of decline and industrial neglect. On a sturdy wooden pallet, the following elements are arranged:
Rusty Barrels: Two metallic barrels covered in rust and stains that add realism and vintage charm. They can be used as storage or decorative elements.
Tires: Worn auto tires with dirty sides, once part of vehicles. They emphasize the theme of abandonment and create an atmosphere of fatigue.
Box: A simple yet intriguing box that raises questions about its fate. We can imagine it as a container for something important or just a forgotten item.
Canister: A dirty canister that might have contained something significant, now lost in the general timelessness of the warehouse.
This 3D model is perfect for themed games, animations, or visualizations aiming to create an ambiance of neglect and abandoned surroundings.

description_text: A castle is a type of fortified structure built during the Middle Ages predominantly by the nobility or royalty and by military orders. Scholars debate the scope of the word castle, but usually consider it to be the private fortified residence of a lord or noble. This is distinct from a palace, which is not fortified; from a fortress, which was not always a residence for royalty or nobility; and from a fortified settlement, which was a public defence – though there are many similarities among these types of construction. Usage of the term has varied over time and has been applied to structures as diverse as hill forts and country houses. Over the approximately 900 years that castles were built, they took on a great many forms with many different features, although some, such as curtain walls, arrowslits, and portcullises, were commonplace.

description_text:
The National Monument (Indonesian: Monumen Nasional, abbreviated Monas) is a 132 m (433 ft) tower in the centre of Merdeka Square, Central Jakarta, symbolizing the fight for Indonesia. It is the national monument of the Republic of Indonesia, built to commemorate the struggle for Indonesian independence.
Construction began in 1961 under the direction of President Sukarno. Monas was opened to the public in 1975. It is topped by a flame covered with gold foil.
The monument and the museum are open daily from 08.00 until 16.00 Western Indonesia Time (UTC+7) throughout the week except for the Mondays when the monument is closed. Since April 2016, the monument also opens during night time, from 19.00 until 22.00 in Tuesday to Friday, and from 19.00 until 00.00 in Saturday and Sunday.[1]

description_text: Dharahara, also called Bhimsen Tower, is a twenty two-storey, 61.88-metre-tall tower at the centre of Sundhara, Kathmandu, Nepal. It was first built in 1832 by Mukhtiyar Bhimsen Thapa under the commission of Queen Lalit Tripurasundari and was a part of the architecture of Kathmandu recognized by UNESCO.The 22-storey rebuilt tower will be inaugurated on April 24, on the eve of the day when the 7.6-magnititude earthquake had rattled the country in 2015.he original one, built by the first prime minister of Nepal Bhimsen Thapa, was destroyed in the 1934 earthquake. Rana Prime minister Juddha Sumsher Rana reconstructed it which was destroyed by the April 2015 earthquake. Under the coordination of the National Reconstruction Authority, the Reconstruction of the monument took place.The inauguration ceremony was organized on the eve of the sixth memorial day of the Gorkha earthquake which occurred on April 25, 2015. Reconstruction of the tower had begun in October 2018. Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli inaugurated the historical Bhimsensthmbha (Dharahara) on April 24, 2021 in Sundhara, Kathmandu.

About the model:

  - The water is a mesh, fixed. (Not animated.)

  - There are two textures sets: One for the ground and other for the Fountain itself. (Base, Roughness, and Normal maps).

  - There is the grass texture included too.

I hope you like it. :)

description_text: In this design, an attempt has been made to use the perspective of the existing contradiction to design the elements of urban furniture. The stillness and suspension of the two paradoxes form a concept that can attract the audience's senses and change the urban mood because what is less felt in our urban spaces today is the same kind of variety and charm that Fermi has. It can create curiosity and mental vitality for the citizens in a constructive and positive direction. The present design's elements are arranged to contrast with our ordinary ideas. Bases that do not seem to be connected and evoke a sense of suspense, chains that, despite the tensile role in the distribution of forces, seemingly play the role of compressive forces, creating a degree of continuity while separating the elements and in a nutshell Creating a new concept of stasis that in its expression reveals a manifestation of geometric instability. It is essential to create a different definition of urban furniture elements in terms of structural expression while maintaining regular use. Creating another presentation from the static one, which at first glance reveals a kind of suspension in space, creates a pleasant mental effect on the citizens. It is worth mentioning that the strength and efficiency of this design have been thoroughly evaluated and do not include any problems due to the lack of a functional purpose in urban furniture as well as damage from the perspective of the impact of vandalism.

The outermost curve circle controls the overall transformation of all objects.
This file retains historical records and does not collapse. The 3D font is easily adjusted.
For UV snapshot, please refer to Preview images on this page.

Maya default renderer: arnold 5.2.1.1.

A set of 6 rocks scanned from real life, all sharing a single texture set of Albedo, AO, Spec-Gloss(PBR) and Normal Map.
You can scale the rocks anywhere between 0.1 and 2.0x in scale for their textures to still hold, additional textures can be overlaid such as a detail mask of moss or more roughness.

All of the rocks are very low poly less than 200 polys per rock.

Extra textures supplied as to get more variation.

description_text:
Compatibility
This is a Bush Plant made for Blender(Cycles-eevee) and Maya (v-ray). It comes with three different variations for each renderer so that your scene doesn't look repetitive.
Polycount
The polygon count is the lowest possible without giving up the quality of a high quality render.  Each  leaf has got 5 vertices, 3 tris. The total polygon count in average of each bush variation is of around 145k tris.
How to use
  - Maya:
All you have to do in maya is to put the maya-version folder in your project folder, and in your scene go to: File>Import and select the .ma version of the desired variation and the model will be placed in your scene with the shaders working correctly, all you have to do than is position it
  - Blender:
All you have to do in blender is to go to File>Append, double click the  .blend file of the variation you want, then open Object folder, and select all the three files inside of it. All you have to do then is position it in your scene, it will be imported with all the shaders ready to go.

description_text:
This is a ground of a Brown and Grey RockTexture, it has been made with Materialize, the textures are in 4096x4096 png files, it is seamless and PBR.
Preview images are screenshot of the material in Materialize.
In the uploaded files, you will find a 3D file where the texture is applied to a plan scaled at 5 with a PBR node, the available formats for it are : .blend, .abc, .dae, .fbx, .glb, .obj, .mtl, .ply, .stl and .x3d. The native is blender so it is in cycles, you ca find the complete node tree in the shader editor. In Blender you just have to shift in the Render Mode to see the displacement of the texture.
Then you will find a .zip file wher are compressed the folowing textures : diffuse, ao, normal, height, metallic, roughness, smoothness and edge. All the texture are not especially necessary to build the texture but I uploaded it anyway in case you would need it. You will find in the .zip file a .mtz load file, if you get Materialize, you can load a project and select this .mtz file to open all the textures in the software.
I am at your disposal if you have any question.
Thanks, enjoy !

description_text:
Car Name: SHC MCE 14
This car is rendered in realtime in Blender Eevee, to open the native Blender file, you will need Blender 2.8.
The price of this car is calculated on it's combination of parts and options in relationship to other MCE cars.The lower priced MCE cars have the same building quality as the higher priced ones, but the overal look and used parts will be better on the higher priced MCE cars.This allows me to release cars at accessable prices, and release better looking ones at a higher price. (all options for this car are listed at the bottom of the description) 
This car is made with the SHC modular car creation tool.
Custom designed parts im a high detailed brandless/generic car with real modern cars inspiration that can be used for renders, presentations, real time apps and video games without displaying or copying any real life car model.
*Detailed exterior
*Detailed interior (can be removed to lower polycount)
*Detailed engine (can be removed to lower polycount)
*Detailed underside
*Materials and textures without shaders are available in the exported files.
*The Studio, materials and camera/door animations are included in the Blender file that is used to create all realtime renders for this car. everything in this file is set up, you only have to move the camera and click ''render''. (roughness is generated with the default texture file)
*The car is linked into several objects to make it more suitable for animations, opening doors, rigging and modifying / tuning / customizing.
*The car is royalty free, so you are free to modify and use it in any (commercial) project as much as you want.
*Objects: 47
File formats: (all file formats are exported with blender 2.8 default settings)*abc *blend *dae *fbx *obj *stl

A crystal or crystalline solid is a solid material whose constituents (such as atoms, molecules, or ions) are arranged in a highly ordered microscopic structure, forming a crystal lattice that extends in all directions. In addition, macroscopic single crystals are usually identifiable by their geometrical shape, consisting of flat faces with specific, characteristic orientations. The scientific study of crystals and crystal formation is known as crystallography. The process of crystal formation via mechanisms of crystal growth is called crystallization or solidification.
The word crystal derives from the Ancient Greek word κρύσταλλος (krustallos), meaning both ice and rock crystal, from κρύος (kruos), icy cold, frost.
Examples of large crystals include snowflakes, diamonds, and table salt. Most inorganic solids are not crystals but polycrystals, i.e. many microscopic crystals fused together into a single solid. Examples of polycrystals include most metals, rocks, ceramics, and ice. A third category of solids is amorphous solids, where the atoms have no periodic structure whatsoever. Examples of amorphous solids include glass, wax, and many plastics.
Despite the name, lead crystal, crystal glass, and related products are not crystals, but rather types of glass, i.e. amorphous solids.
Crystals are often used in pseudoscientific practices such as crystal therapy, and, along with gemstones, are sometimes associated with spellwork in Wiccan beliefs and related religious movements.

This is a Cyan, Dark Blue, Purple and Pink Extraterrestrial Ground Texture, it has been made with Materialize, the textures are in 4096x4096 png files, it is seamless and PBR.
The preview images are screenshot of the material in Materialize, the first one has been made in Blender Cycles Render.
In the uploaded files, you will find a 3D file where the texture is applied to a plan scaled at 2 with a PBR node. You will find in the .zip file a .mtz load file, if you get Materialize, you can load a project and select this .mtz file to open all the textures in the software.
I am at your disposal if you have any question.
Thanks !

Later the construction of a new building begins at the intersection of Maipú and San Juan streets in the form of 15-story tower with 30 apartments and three local, completed in 1943 was one of the first high-rise buildings of the city and 1986 was expanded with the construction of a confectionery. The designers were Picasso Tower, Fernandez Days and Funes. The construction company was to Muniagurria, Arroyo and Spillet, the front, the balconies of the first 6 floors and the hall are clad in travertine marble and the doors are of polished cedar. Maglev routes are mostly on land and traverse the oceans only to the shortest routes. On the USA- Europe route, for example, the longest water transverse end section is only about 500 Km long. Energy is supplied enviroment- friendly by waterpowered sea flow power plants every 450m.The magnetic levitation drive automatically. description_text:
A LowPoly trade tent with easily removable objects from the tent itself.
Easily importable to Unity or any other game engine etc. with the materials on them. Easily switch materials (may be duplicates if added to game engines, but that's an easy fix), and also if you don't want the bottles or any other object on the table, you can easily remove the child objects of the tent (which is the parent object), for example I have added a picture what it looks like in Unity, easily move, remove or duplicate/edit the parts you want, add more barrels or remove them etc.
Tent itself is 1062 verts. and 1059 faces
Barrel: 182 verts., 171 faces (total of 11 barrels, 2 under the tent desk and rest beside the tent)
Chest: 290 verts., 270 faces (total of 3 chests, one smaller on the table, one larger under  table, and one open with 2 bottles inside (bottles give extra verts/faces).
Bottle: 110 verts. 102 faces. (total of 20 bottles not counting the ones inside the chest which are joined to that chest-object)
Shield = 512 verts. 482 faces (total of 6 shields)
Axe = 134 verts, 120 faces

The 3D  fire hydrant model was created on real base. It's created accurately, in  real units of measurement, qualitatively and maximally close to the  original.

Model formats:
- *.max (3ds Max)
- *.fbx (Multi Format)
- *.obj (Multi Format)
- *.3ds (Multi Format)
- *.blend (Blender 2.79)
- *.c4d (Cinema 4D 17)
* renders Are made in Cinema 4D R17
If you need any other formats we are more than happy to make them for you.

The  model is provided combined, all main parts are presented as separate  parts therefore materials of objects are easy to be modified or removed  and standard parts are easy to be replaced. If you experience  difficulties with separating standard parts we are more than happy to  give you qualified assistance. Thank you for picking interest in my  models. 
The archive texture folder is included.

description_text:
A kerosene lamp is a type of lighting device that uses kerosene as a fuel. Invented by the Polish pharmacist Ignacy Łukasiewicz in 1853, kerosene lamps have a wick or mantle as light source, protected by a glass chimney or globe; lamps may be used on a table, or hand-held lanterns may be used for portable lighting. Like oil lamps, they are useful for lighting without electricity, such as in regions without rural electrification, in electrified areas during power outages, at campsites, and on boats. There are three types of kerosene lamp: flat-wick, central-draught (tubular round wick), and mantle lamp. Kerosene lanterns meant for portable use have a flat wick and are made in dead-flame, hot-blast, and cold-blast variants.

History
The Golden Gate (in Spanish, Golden Door) is a suspension bridge located in California, the United States, that unites the peninsula of San Francisco by the north with the south of the county of Marin, near Sausalito. Golden Gate is also the name of the strait in which the bridge is built, and gets its name from the Strait in Constantinople, also called the Golden Gate, as it communicated Europe with Asia.
The Golden Gate is the most famous bridge in San Francisco despite not being the largest in this city, since the Bay Bridge is the main road.

description_text:
A simple and low-poly Indian Letter Box for any street envirtonment, perfect as a decor item. The renders in the preview were produced by Keyshot . The preview images also contains wireframe images alongside few images and non-edited textured images directly taken from Maya's viewport. 
Since both of the core models are same, their UV's are overlapped in order to save UV space and give both of them greater texel density.  To keep things lightweight, all the details are fused in a single diffuse texture map. 
Due to the low poly nature, they can be used in mobile games as well as any simulation.
**Note: Materials are not provided and textures are not embedded. The model only has a default material from Maya, it would be best if you could attach your own material and apply the provided texture image for best results. **
If you have any queries or require any form of assistance, feel free to give me a message (:

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 The College Cult of Science (currently EE Cult of Science) is a high school education in the Botafogo neighborhood in the city of Campinas, São Paulo, Brazil. It was founded in January 12, 187, as a private school for boys by a named association Society Cult of Science, where the members made to the Masonic Lodge Independence. Composed of farmers, merchants and intellectuals of the city, among them were: Antonio Pompeu de Camargo; Francisco Glicério, Sales Courses that later would become president of Brazil 1898-1902), Jorge Krug; Boniface Joaquim do Amaral, the Viscount of Indaiatuba, Joaquim Egidio de Souza Aranha, the Marquis of Three Rivers; Cândido Ferreira, and the Baron of Atibaia. The school name reflects the influence of positivism of its founders. In 1890 the school went through a crisis and had to close its doors until 1896, when it was reopened under the aegis of the government of São Paulo as State Gymnasium. Until 1964, when a controversial education reform was promoted by the military regime, the Cult to Science College was an equal and high-quality school, frequented both by the economic elite and the middle class.

description_text: It occupies a land with 1.554m² trapezoid-shaped, with the straight forward and curled back, keeping certain similarities with another project made by the architect during this time: the Copan building in Sao Paulo. It has 15 floors and 60 apartments. It is a building with its own characteristics and almost unique in the city: ceiling height of 3 meters, extensive use of louvers on both sides of building and urban design that was unconfigured over time: initially there were no walls or railings around the building, with free access between Sister Serafina Avenue (front) and Rua Coronel Brill (rear), integrating the public space to particular through the use of stilts on the ground floor. Increased urban insecurity demanded the removal of this typical feature of modern architecture and niemeyeriana.

description_text:
La mosquée Hassan-II arabe : مسجد الحسن الثاني (masjid al-Hassan ath-thani)) est une mosquée située à Casablanca (Maroc). Érigée en partie sur la mer, elle est un complexe religieux et culturel, aménagé sur neuf hectares et comporte une salle de prières , une salle d'ablutions, des bains, une école coranique  (madrasa), une bibliothèque [archive] et un musée.
La salle de prière  peut accueillir 25 000 fidèles1 d'une superficie totale de 20 000 m2. et l'esplanade 80 000 fidèles (l'ensemble complet peut accueillir 105 000 personnes).
La mosquée Hassan-II  est l'une des plus grandes mosquées du monde, et possède un minaret d'une hauteur de 200 1 à 210 m3 selon les sources, le plus haut du monde. Des artisans recrutés dans toutes les villes du royaume avaient sculpté 53 000 m2 de bois et assemblé plus de 10 000 m2 de zellige (céramiques) pour le lieu de culte.
Un toit ouvrant  de grande dimension permet, selon le vœu du roi Hassan II, de relier cet édifice à l'air, considéré comme l'un des quatre éléments bénéfiques à la vie, avec la terre, le feu et l'eau.
Conçue par l'architecte Michel Pinseau, elle a été édifiée par le groupe français Bouygues.

The character was co-created by writer and editor Stan Lee, developed by screenwriter Larry Lieber and designed by artists Don Heck and Jack Kirby. He made his first appearance in Tales of Suspense # 39 (March 1963), and received his own title in Iron Man # 1 (May 1968).
Anthony Edward Stark, better known as Tony Stark, a wealthy American business magnate, playboy and witty scientist, suffers a serious chest injury during a kidnapping. When his captors try to force him to build a weapon of mass destruction he creates, instead, a powerful armor to save his life and escape from captivity. Later, Stark develops his suit, adding weapons and other technological devices that he designed through his company, Stark Industries. He uses the suit and the successive versions to protect the world as Iron Man. Although at first he concealed his true identity, Stark finally declared that he was, in fact, Iron Man in a public announcement.

Here we have one park bench with PBR wood Texture. 
Designed by me for a project I'm doing, it's acurately modelled to comparable Park Bench dimensions.
The model was buit in on Rhino 6 with V-Ray 3.6, but other formats are attached, including High & Low Poly mesh. PDF Notes are included & can be downloaded seperately.
The Rhino 6/V-ray Model is archived with it's packed V-ray materials & ready to go once unzipped.
The PBR Textures are  Archived in a folder marked Park Bench Textures. More details attached to the PDF with the model.
Other included file formats:
FBX, 3DS (High & Low Poly), OBJ (High & Low Poly), Lightwave (High & Low Poly), IGS **Please Note: **Some of the formats will not have material properties/layers & so you may have to map & assign these manually.MTL Files are included.
Dimensions of bench:  W 150 cm H 90cm D 66cm
Any feedback is always welcome.
Thanks for Looking!
Eclectic Design

description_text:
Low-Poly Minecraft Diamond Sword made in Blender. Used texture. You can download the texture I shared between preview images. Zip file includes texture too. Game-Ready 3D model. 
Minecraft is a sandbox video game developed by Mojang. The game was created by Markus Notch Persson in the Java programming language. Following several early test versions, it was released as a paid public alpha for personal computers in 2009 before releasing in November 2011, with Jens Bergensten taking over development. Minecraft has since been ported to several other platforms and is the best-selling video game of all time, with 200 million copies sold and 126 million monthly active users as of 2020.
In Minecraft, players explore a blocky, procedurally-generated 3D world with infinite terrain, and may discover and extract raw materials, craft tools and items, and build structures or earthworks. Depending on game mode, players can fight computer-controlled mobs, as well as cooperate with or compete against other players in the same world. Game modes include a survival mode, in which players must acquire resources to build the world and maintain health, and a creative mode, where players have unlimited resources. Players can modify the game to create new gameplay mechanics, items, and assets.
Minecraft has been critically acclaimed, winning several awards and being cited as one of the greatest video games of all time. Social media, parodies, adaptations, merchandise, and the annual MineCon conventions played large roles in popularizing the game. It has also been used in educational environments, especially in the realm of computing systems, as virtual computers and hardware devices have been built in it. In 2014, Mojang and the Minecraft intellectual property were purchased by Microsoft for US$2.5 billion. A number of spin-off games have also been produced, such as Minecraft: Story Mode, Minecraft Dungeons, and Minecraft Earth. 
Thank you for Downloading.

description_text:
Here we have one Picnic-Table of the type you might find outside a pub or restraurant. 
The model 
This model was created on Rhino 6 as a NURBS model and rendered in V-Ray Next, but I have uploaded multiple file formats in Polygon Mesh.All materials & maps are included as well as Rhino MTL material files. So if you don't have V-ray you can still get a good render.
*Included file formats: *

  - 3DS -High & Low Poly mesh. All textures & materials are included & so are PDF notes. (Also see Preview images)

  - OBJ -High & Low Poly mesh

  - OBJ -MTL Files

  - LWO -High & Low Poly mesh

  - STEP

  - IGES

  - SKP (2013)

  - The Rhino 6/V-ray Model is archived with it's packed V-ray materials & ready to go once unzipped.

  - Vray Scene file (VRSCENE) which comes embedded with all textures & materials. VRSCENE files are compatible accross different platforms running Vray, more info can be found on the PDF.

Dimensions : W 150 cm H 78cm  L 150cm 
Any feedback is always welcome.
Thanks for Looking!
Eclectic Design

description_text: The Control Feed Silo is 22.4 m in diameter. It has 3 days stock. The raw mill product is put into this silo. The outlet has 7 pressure relieving cones. These cones open up in sequence. 3 at a time and are air-rated, in order to have proper mixing. Below the deck slab there is another air mixing chamber called the mixing bin. It is supported on Load cells. From here the material passes through the schenk feeders (For controlling the amount of flow). Then it goes to the bucket elevators (One stand-by) to be fed into the preheater system. The Air slides are split into the two strings and has a bottom outlet in order to have a re circulating back into the silo.

description_text:
[BACKGROUND]
The bicycle has been around for hundreds of years. It was at the center of one of the earliest technological races in human history. Over the hundreds of years since its creation, the bicycle has remained fairly unchanged in its most basic form.  As a bond of human power and technology, the bicycle enabled humans to travel far beyond what they had been able to previously by foot. As with all things regarding speed, human became obsessed with pushing the limits of both technology and human ability. This mentality led to the racing of bicycles. 2014 marked the 101st edition of the Tour de France and the 107th edition of Paris-Roubaix, two of greatest cycling races of all time. With Such a long history of cycling as a sport, it is clear that it is unlikely the sport will ever disappear.
[VELODROME DEFINED]velodrome (ˈviːləˌdrəʊm; ˈvɛl-)n1. (Cycle Racing) an arena with a banked track for cycle racing
[THE PROJECT]
Velodrome 2114 is a visualization of a sporting atmosphere in the future rather than the present. With time, all things change and Architecture is no exception. As time has progressed there has been a clear contrast in two major directions of progressive architecture. The first mimicking the natural world and its organic forms and the second with its sharply designed edges and sleek facades. For Velodrome 2114, the second approach was chosen in order to mirror the technological advancements within cycling itself. Over the past decade, racing bicycles have become the centerpiece of aerodynamic and structural studies. So much so, companies known for creating the fastest cars on the planet have become involved. However, looking past all the advancements of cycling, the most basic shape in a bicycle frame is the triangle and thus it is a centerpiece in the design of Velodrome 2114. As humans we will always look to compete whether it is in technology or sports and it is because of this desire for competition that sports will always remain an integral part of human culture. Events such as the Olympics will remain and therefore, there will be a need for new facilities at every Olympiad for each discipline of sport. Thus we have Velodrome 2114.

description_text:
This is a double shell, solar-vented cool birdhouse for the Birdhouse Challenge, printable in one piece.  Your chicks will thank you! 
There is a drain at the bottom and a ring of ventilation holes at the bottom and top of the inner shell, and another ring of slots and holes at the bottom and top of the outer shell.  Any sunlight on the outer shell sets up a convection cycle with cooler air being drawn in through the lower ring of slots and rising to exit the large holes, so the inner shell and nest remain cooler.  A post and ring joins the two shells at the top for a sturdy hanger.  The roof, lack of a perch, and gap between shells makes it difficult for a predator to reach the eggs or chicks.  There's no bird bath because chicks won't appreciate the resulting disturbance or encouragement of predators, and the opening is high enough that the chicks won't fall out before they are ready.  

Please let me know how you do!  

I used drsfostersmith.com/pic/article.cfm?aid=2194 as a guide to design.  Sizing - check.  Heating and cooling - check, but there's no insulation for winter except to cover exterior holes to trap dead air.  Proper drainage - check.  Safety - check, while there's no metal plate, there are two openings that would have to be enlarged, and a squirrel would have trouble hanging on anyway.  Mounting and access - check/fail.  There is no cleanout plug - you'll have to use a hooked wire and fish out all the nesting materials to clean it out.

description_text:
I added 3 plexiglas sides to keep the heat in my Solidoodle 3 to assist with ABS printing.  Very simple - 2 hooks, a knob, and a neodymium magnet superglued to the top.  I ended up using the knob only on the front piece.  

Cut three 13" x 13" square sheets of plastic - I recommend 1/4" thick if you're going out to get it, but it can be 1/8" or 3/16" or 3/8" if you have the scrap.  

Mount the two clips on the bottom at the corners (shown in photo), and glue a magnet to each near the top.  A 1/8" thick magnet and the clips will leave about 1/8" gap all around, plenty for the various screws and rivets on the Solidoodle.  If you're using a Solidoodle 2, you'll need to reduce the size to fit, but the clips should work as-is.  

To remove, simply lift up the plexiglas - the magnet slides easier than it pulls off - and then pick off the sheet.

description_text:
Wardenclyffe Tower (1901–1917) also known as the Tesla Tower, was an early wireless transmission tower designed by Nikola Tesla (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Tesla) in Shoreham, New York and intended for commercial trans-Atlantic wireless telephony, broadcasting, and proof-of-concept demonstrations of wireless power transmission. It was never fully operational, and the tower was demolished in 1917.
The tower was named after James S. Warden, a western lawyer and banker who had purchased land for the endeavor in Shoreham, Long Island, about sixty miles from Manhattan. Here he built a resort community known as Wardenclyffe-On-Sound. Warden believed that with the implementation of Tesla's "world system" a "Radio City" would arise in the area. He offered Tesla 200 acres (81 ha) of land close to a railway line on which to build his wireless telecommunications tower and laboratory facility.

Hello fellow modelers, this is a model I've spent only a little amount of time on as a gift to anyone working on a Afghanistan/Africa application.  Please if you download this and enjoy it as a free product please LIKE on the page for me.  Keep an eye out for other products I will be posting for free.
After a work project I had to use Afghani homes/villages for a few scenes. This is a common Collade which is typically made of a mixture of mud and straw making better insulatin then a wood structure. The model is a C4D native file and is preset for Subdivision rendering, all other file formats come with 2 versions a low res and high res model depending on the scene you are trying to place this in.
The material is a multi-layer creation of turbulence and bump mapping that gives a nice rough apperance in sunlight.
The models are editable and contain mostly quads for nice mesh subdivision. Ready to fit into your scene.
NOTE: All my models have a mixture of Quads, Tri's.NOTE: All renderings are performed using C4D and do not necessarily reflect other programs materials or rendering results.

description_text:
I needed a scale model of a house so what would be better to make one of your own. This is the house i grew up in and my parents still live there.
I looked up the original drawings (which by the way are about than 100 years old) from the house i grew up in, scanned them and used them to sketch the house in CAD. I tried to keep the model simple enough but still keep a certain level of detail.
The model is at 1:87 scale (same as some model trains).

description_text:

Go to a ladder component and hold the e-key to climb up, down or sideways.
Every ladder component has a property called ladder and the PlayerBox searches for this property
with a near-sensor.
Every time you near to an object that contains the ladder property you get a gameinfo E-Key on the screen so you know that you can climb.
P-Key.................Starts the Game Engine
W-Key.................Move forwards
S-Key.................Move backwards
D-Key.................Move to the right
A-Key.................Move to the left
Hold Spacebar.........Player moves faster
Q-Key.................Jump
F-Key.................Changed the daytime forward
B-Key.................Changed the daytime backward
E-Key.................Climb up

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 6 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Tower 42 (still commonly known by its previous name, Natwest Tower) Is the tallest building in the city of London and the third tallest building in London as a whole. Tower 42 was built in 1980 and took 6 year to build. The building has 47 floors and stands at a fairly impressive 183m tall. On completion the building was the tallest building in London until the topping out of One Canada Square in Canary Wharf. The tower features an expensive seafood and champagne bar on the 42nd floor called Vertigo 42 which featured as the ending point to the Top Gear challenge where a Bugatti Veyron raced a private plane across Western Europe. Although suspected to represent the logo of the Natwest Tower from the air, something that Natwest utilised in television adverts, the architect Richard Seifert always denied his design was supposed to embody Natwest's logo.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 6 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 122 Leadenhall Street is currently under demolition (Sep 07) to make way for the new 224m tall Leadenhall Building. The building is being unusually being demolished by McGee that has created a building which seemingly hovers in mid-air. This is due to the top down construction that has a central core supporting a crown that works as a cantilever to support the floors slung under it hence the need to demolish the lowest floors and work up. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Facts-   Tower 42 (then known as the NatWest Tower) was the tallest building in the United Kingdom for 10 years, from its completion in 1980 to the topping-out of One Canada Square in November 1990.  

  - National Westminster Bank initially planned a tower of 137m (450ft), but after it retained Richard Seifert as chief architect in 1964 he submitted a preliminary design at 197m (647ft). The proposal called for demolition of two historic buildings - the City of London Club (1834) and the small National Provincial Bank. After prolonged investigation, in 1964 the Environmental Secretary upheld a preservation order on the banking hall, but permitted demolition of the City of London Club, and the tower's height was reduced to 183m (600ft).

  - On completion, Tower 42 was the world's tallest cantilevered building.

  - External cleaning of the building is provided in part by an automated mechanical cleaning system.

  - The three cantilevered sections hang from the building's central core and are asymmetrical in height.

This pit is going through the underwater and underground of the ocean bottom, and in there is lets the plane smash into the ground and explode. On this scene, you see how this planes are being pulled into the pit (thanx to AirbusA330 for the planes, and different users for the effects on the crashes [forgot]). The most interesting part of this facility, is that it is built near Hawaii, and that makes the danger of the planes being exploded and destroyed is high, because if they crash the facility, the building will go underwater, and create a self-tsunami. The runway has symbols showing what to do, and then they are being controlled on the computer. The only thing that the computer controls is the ailerons, and because of that the plane may spin out of control and the only thing you do is position the plane in horizontal position. L-300 is being tested right now, and has paint on them to difer different kinds of flaps, speedbrakes, and some other things with them. If the plane brakes apart too early, when it doesn't hit the gap that is opened, then the plane is not going to be flying anymore, or will just not be. L-300, didn't hit the gap. It is no more flying. L-200, did hit the gap. New investigation result, the plane was over-pressured by the pilots. Pilots' Mistake.

This one is pretty complicated: it has an interior of boxes and those holding peels. This is one of my best models so far. Nerlerit Inaat Airport is located in Greeland. It is very small, so here`s some info about it from Wikipedia: Nerlerit Inaat Airport (Kalaallisut: Mittarfik Nerlerit Inaat, Danish: Constable Pynt Lufthavn) (IATA: CNP, ICAO: BGCO) is an airport in the Sermersooq municipality in eastern Greenland. It is located on Jameson Land and serves the town of Ittoqqortoormiit, approximately 40 km (25 mi) to the south-east. The airport can serve STOL aircraft. A Bell 222 helicopter of Air Greenland is permanently housed at the airport, linking it with Ittoqqortoormiit Heliport. The helicopter also provides search and rescue capabilities within the surrounding area, and can be chartered for transport. The airport may be relocated to a new site on Liverpool Land closer to Ittoqqortoormiit, between the settlement and Uunarteq cape (Danish: Kap Tobin) to the south, thus eliminating the need for helicopter transfers. The airport acts as stopping off point for a number of expeditions into Jameson Land and Northeast Greenland National Park. Areas such as Renland have only just been visited, or have had no known visitors. In summer 2004 the airport was the destination of an arctic trip by two German microlight pilots flying a Flight Design CT2K light aircraft.

Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This is the terminals of Saint Maarten {St. Martin/St. Maarten}. Including jetways. This is free for edits.    Princess Juliana International Airport (IATA: SXM, ICAO: TNCM) (also known as Saint Maarten International Airport) serves the Dutch part of the island of Saint Martin. In 2007, the airport handled 1,647,824 passengers and 103,650 aircraft movements. The airport serves as a hub for Windward Islands Airways and is the major gateway for the smaller Leeward Islands, including Anguilla, Saba, St. Barthélemy and St. Eustatius. It is named after Juliana of the Netherlands, who as crown princess landed here in 1944, the year after the airport opened. There is also an airport on the French side of the island, called Aéroport de Grand Case or L'Espérance Airport.    Minister of Justice, Roland Duncan and Deputy Prime Minister Theo Heyliger are undertaking plans to create a hub for Anguilla and St. Barths by placing both Anguillan and French official immigration officers in order to facilitate travel to these areas.    The airport was started as a military airstrip in 1942. It was converted to a civilian airport in 1943. In 1964 the airport was remodeled and relocated, with a new terminal building and control tower. The facilities were upgraded in 1985 and 2001.

description_text:
This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 OH. MY. GOD. BEST. THING. EVER!!!Don’t ask how many hours I have been searching for textures for this thing. Forever it seems like {actually for a couple months now}.This is the Hekla Aurora, a 757 especially painted in this beautiful color scheme of Aurora Borealis in Iceland. It is the first model that I ever published that features no intersections [it’s full texture, except the tail where I had to invert the text on the right side of the aircraft]. Full texture, no doors, no windows, only the windshield. Thanks to AirbusA330 and AirplaneNerd777 for the template. I have finally done it, I can’t believe my own eyes.Icelandair is the main airline of Iceland, headquartered at Reykjavík Airport in Reykjavík. It is part of the Icelandair Group and currently operates scheduled services to 35 cities in 16 countries on both sides of the Atlantic Ocean out of its hub at Keflavík International Airport. The geographical position of Iceland allows one-stop transatlantic flights, which are one pillar of the airline's business strategy, along with traffic to and from the country. In 2012, Icelandair transported 2,021,000 passengers, an increase of 16%25 compared to 2011. Icelandair has upgraded the cockpit of their Boeing 757-200s and -300s with state of the art full glass cockpit. Icelandair announced the order for 4 Boeing 787 Dreamliners. In 2011 it was announced that 3 orders will be transferred to Norwegian Air Shuttle. On December 6, 2012, the airline committed itself to ordering the upcoming Boeing 737 MAX aircraft, 8 of which will be the MAX 8, and 4 will be the MAX 9. On 13 February, 2013 ,the airlines finalized the order for 16 Boeing 737 MAX 8s and Boeing 737 MAX 9s, in addition 8 purchase rights for Boeing 737 MAX aircraft. On the 9th of December Icelandair revealed a Boeing 757-256, TF-FIU, In a new Northern Lights Livery.  In February 2015, Icelandair launched a northern lights themed Boeing 757 named Hekla Aurora as part of the company’s %232MyStopover campaign. The exterior, which was hand-painted by a team of highly skilled airbrush artists from the UK, features remarkable artwork depicting an Icelandic winter scene complete with beautiful northern lights. Inside the plane, an impressive installation of LED mood lighting continues the theme by emulating both the colours and dancing patterns of the aurora. As part of Icelandair’s transatlantic fleet, the Hekla Aurora flies to all of the airline’s 39 destinations and has a three-day schedule available for passengers and observers. 
EDIT: HOTFIX: replaced landing gear. Thanks to dre737 :) EDIT2: added %232MyStopover on inner side of winglets; fixed “dividing polygon” issue; made compatible thumbnail.

This is one of CrystallisAero's destinations, so that's why I decided to post this as my last GE model :) . Maota Airport [IATA: MXS, ICAO: NSMA] is the main domestic airport on the island of Savai'i in Samoa. It is situated near Salelologa at the east end of Savai'i. The airport is located 10 minutes south of Salelologa township and ferry terminal. The airport has been in operation since the early 1990s. It services flights from Faleolo International Airport on the main island Upolu and Asau Airport at the northwest end of Savai'i. The airport has a short runway which can only handle Twin Otters and other small passenger aircraft. There is a reasonable tarmac that could actually fit a Boeing 737. However, the airport terminal, an open fale, is small. Planes are forbidden to land or take off at night due to a lack of lighting. A small control tower exists, however, it still needs assistance from the main base in Faleolo International Airport on Upolu island.

This one happened to be renovated from its original 4 bedroom, 1 bathroom version to 3 bedrooms and 2.5 bathrooms. This is not a Sears Home, though, it is a Gordon Van Tine Home. It is similar to a foursquare house though people may not call it that. Like any kit home, you'd walk into a great big living room, beyond, a dining room, then a kitchen in the far back corner. Basement stairs would be below the main stair. The laundry room used to be the pantry. The furnace is in the basement, then rides a chase up through the house in the form of a chimney. The building itself, built in the 20's is a relic of mail-order homes mass produced for the growth of cities. Sit on its grand porch, the signature item, or in the singanature bay window upstairs. Either way, you might like to live in this home. It is an 8-minute bus ride to downtown Paulwall or in 10 minute walking proximity to the Paulwall College main campus. This is also near a busy shopping center. The house is in a neighborhood full of other beautifully preserved old homes with tree-lined streets. Enjoy and please rate :)

This is the second tallest building in the city, standing at 15 civilian floors but with two plant floors above, making it 17 stories high. A building completed/opened in 1968, it does have stories to tell for it changed hands several times. It was originally Paulwall National Bank but it went bankrupt a bout 15 years ago, then Wells Fargo bought the building a decade ago. Wells Fargo bank lives on the first couple of stories, then the upper floors are rented to tenants to house offices and general business. There is an accounting office up there, a printing office, publishing office, law firm, and even a credit union. A few floors remain empty as they await tenants. So nothing unlike a regular office building in any downtown setting. In terms of banking, Paulwall has a good multitude of different banks all around the city. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This is perhaps Paulwall's most famous and fanciest office structures within city limits. It is one of the few Paulwall buildings to make the National Register of Historic Places. The building bears the Santa Fe letters, making it known as the Santa fe Building. No, this building is not in Santa Fe but it is along the Santa Fe railroad, once owned by the Santa Fe company. This is one of the biggest buildings in Paulwall, only 2 other structures are taller making this the 3rd tallest in Paulwall. There are 13 floors! One of the first things commuters see when passing through Paulwall on the freeway. It is a gothic revival building. It is about 100 years old! Street level contains 3 storefronts and a small business lobby. Floors 2-12 house offices for business. Accountants, credit unioun, consultants, attourneys, publishing, corporate headquarters and even a marraige license office is in this building along with other county offices. The 13th story penthouse is a restaraunt. The most expensive restaraunt in all of Paulwall, the kind where you have to wear a suit and tie. Well, this building is the architectural crown for downtown Paulwall, packed with details! Enjoy :)

Paulwall has several of these transfer stations including this one from downtown. See, someone gets off a bus here then waits for another one. The shelter has additional benches inside along with a map of Paulwall and the marked bus routes. It is there for when unfavorable weather like wind, rain, or snow so people don't have to wait in the weather for their ride. description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 13 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Welcome to the famed Paulwall Teapot, the largest teapot in all of Paulwall. Well, and the most abandoned one too! What could be sadder? Who would abandon their teapot like that? Well, obviously someone who's invested business in Paulwall for a while. The teapot, built in 1922, is Paulwall's oldest standing gas station. Yes, used to house the fuel to get your cars on the road! Such historical significance but as like several other historically significant structures in Paulwall, they went vacant. But this is one of the last standing buildings left on its block. There used to be 2 motels (across street), both gone, a neon tin-clad silver diner (next door) which is also gone as well as the vanishing of other stores and houses. There used to be large industrial warehouse type structures behind this teapot that are now gone so because all those buildings are gone, from here to the train tracks, you'd get an uninterrupted view of the buildings of downtown Paulwall. Creepy area to be at night, never go alone and probably shouldn't get out of your car either. Holes in the pavement on each side of the gas pumps show where the canopy used to be. The station changed hands so you don't see the original retro pumps. Abandoned since the 90's. Enjoy and please rate :)

The house has formal dining and a living room divided by a stone wall. The living room boasts a warm fire place. The kitchen is HUGE complete with island and stainless steel appliances and a walk-in pantry. There is a breakfast room too as part of the kitchen. The master suite is grand with exposed rafters, a vaulted ceiling, and a huge picture window. There are 3 other bedrooms upstairs along with a bonus area with lots of glass The basement is complete. It is there to divide the motorcycle stall from the regular car stalls -I just decided to use one big garage door for both stalls. The stall on the left can fit 2 cars, one in first, the second one after (explains why it is so deep). The stall on the right is for a single car. And the one in the middle, again, the motorcycle stall. The big room down there has a small kitchen. It could be used as a atudio, oversized rumpus room (essentially a bonus/ game room), or rent it out, up to you! My favorite parts are probably the decks out back and the spiral staircase. There is probably something in this house for everyone. Enjoy and please rate. Follow the link below for my new Facebook Page :)

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Here is a geodesic dome as a residence to live in! It is an unusual house on the eastern edge of Paulwall. Paulwall has a few domes, actually, each with a distinct floor plan. A geodesic dome is expensive to build but is worth half the cost to heat and cool of a traditional box house. This is made of hexagons and pentagons. Interesting how they aren't really much thicker than traditional walls, and with wall studs, shapes hinged together. This house is great for the Paulwall area for there are severe storm threats every spring. Perfectly flat land in the middle of open prarie... The house is also impervious to earthquakes though Paulwall is not in a siesmic zone. The modern house is different from traditional modeling though the traditional layers are the same so you can explore with ease. 3 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms. There are other domes used as a cabin or a vacation house. Some call it a hobbit's bungalow. Could it be the house of a famous soccer player? Your choice! I hope you enjoy this dome house and please rate. The Facebook page with lots of architecture is found at my link below. Enjoy :)

This house is a hybrid between the modern face of the outside and the old fashoined country-style interior. This house has a lot of detail inside out. It features 3 bedrooms, 2.5 bathrooms, 2 living areas, pantry in the kitchen, a laundry room with vaccum cleaner closet, and includes the water heater. There is no basement but there is storage under the stairs. The family room features a sloped ceiling with the upstairs hall directly above. The living room's fireplace features spark arresters. My personally favorite room in the house is the master bedroom. It has a chair rail with stained wood paneling and wallpaper. There are his and her closets on either side of the window. The ideal location, I'll say is a Colorado mountain community, but you are free to put it wherever. There are plenty of skylights, a grilling patio out back (covered by a pergola), and guess what, the house is even solar! Enjoy and please rate. Layers make it easier to explore. Take a careful look about the exterior. Not much right? Then, I invite you to see inside! The barn's interior features 28 cow stalls complete with scrape alleys and mangers. There are 4 sets of stalls meaning there are 4 alleys and mangers. There are 6 passage ways surrounding the sets for easy access and circulation. There are four apartments on each floor and every single room has a window to the outside! 100 years ago, these apartments were built to house as many people as possible, sometimes a whole family shared a single room. That was when there was a massive flood of imigrants in the U.S.A.. The rooms can be accessed. To see one unit by itself, turn off the tenement row layer. Each apartment has a wood-stove but no bathroom. Each floor has two toilets and one washroom across from the stairs. Every apartment has access to a fire escape. Take a look at the air shafts (in between each unit), scroll mouldings, rear yard, window mouldings, and the bars on the first story windows! Please rate the model. Everyone shall enjoy this, probably the greatest of my models to date!

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 This prarie style house is sort of an American four square house. It actually looks like it has some Frank Lloyd Wright influences in the architecture. It is worth looking around at. When entering, you are greated by a nice looking staircase, all stained hardwood and a built-in cusioned bench. There is a nice large living room, the biggest room in the house with a broad brick fire place. It has a unique private porch. Beyond is the formal dining room which is also pretty big for a house like this. The kitchen is fairly self explainitory. The pantry has counter space and some overhead cupboards. Upstairs features 4 bedrooms with the home's only bathroom. The master bedroom is obviously the largest along with 2 closets and a fireplace of its own. The stairs are sort of unusual. There is a dualling staircase made for the servants (so guests wouldn't see them). Back in the turn-of-the century, when there were guests, all the guests got to see of the house were the parlor and the dining room. Everything else was strictly off limits for them. This is a catalog house from Sears %26 Roebuck back in 1913. Imagine you living in a mail-order house. There are two accesses to the basement; one out back and one below the staircase. There were to be stairs to the atic from above the servant's staircase but I will have to play a little more with the house to get it right. One day, I'll change it but in the mean time, please do enjoy this house. I would love for you to rate and comment.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Here is one building of a 6-building housing project. I modeled this tall apartment house after the famous Brewster Wheeler Housing Project in Detroit Michigan Near downtown. I understand this is the year these tall buildings along with some townhouses will be demolished by the city but I liked the designs so I modeled it. This is the tallest building in Paulwall standing at 15 stories in counting! If you are wondering about the first floor, it is sunken into the ground by a few feet. The vestibule has a few steps leading downward. No apartments on the first floor, just the second and so on up. Turn the roof layer off to see the top floor. 8 apartments, a trash room, mechanical room (empty), mail chute, stairs, and an elevator shaft. Each house has 2 small bedrooms, walk-in pantry, one bathroom, and so on. I modeled this old house using whatever photos I could find online as well as watching the videos about it. Diana Ross and the Supremes lived here for a little while. It was the first subsidized house in America for African Americans. Completed in 1952. I hope you enjoy this old house and please rate. Though the actual thing exists in Detroit, you may feel free to put it into your inner city. You can remove the apartments and make it a background object if you like :)

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Here is a medium sized bungalow with 3 bedrooms and one bathroom. It was built from a line of Harris kit homes from the 10's, 20's, and 30's. These houses are hugely common on the outskirts of norhtern metropolises. Common enough that these homes are placed in long rows, your house would look just like your neighbors' with either the same or similar floor plan. The house was made with its exact dimentions. I used his sections, scaled floor plan, and whatever pictures I've scrounged off the internet (lots). Upstairs has 3 small bedrooms with built-in beds and one bathroom. A particular acknowledgement would be the famous origami chairs in the living room. Although they were not in the origional plan, they were added later, sitting there today. They were modeled by my good friend, Jeff Myers (JATdesigns) however, everything else was crafted by me. Enjoy this model. The layers will make it easy for you. I hope you have as much fun looking through it as I had in making it. I have a Facebook Page now :)

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 It is a 40's tract house. These houses were very common in the United States in cities used mainly by the working class and incoming veterans. In this time period, there was a skyrocket in the demand for housing so many houses were needed in a short time. Tract homes were very cookie cutter so you would step out onto your porch to see a copy of your house across the street. However, the homes weren't all the same. They varied by neighborhood and time period. It was common that tract homes had 2 bedrooms but this model actually has 4. It also has 2 full bathrooms (another rare comfort)! There is a basement. I am not a fan of tract-style kitchens so I designed the kitchen. It is designed for the tabe to be right there in the kitchen. There is a wroght iron column in front along with a living room picture window. There is good clost space here. The chimney is actually the furnace vent trailing all the way to the basement. These houses most commonly found near factories or jumbled around downtown. Either way, I hope you enjoy this tract house. Please rate. For more houses and architecture, don't forget to check out my Facebook page given at the link below.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Here is a surviving cabin left from the abandoned Camp Paulwall. It was a boys' summer camp off of the bank of the Paulwall River. The camp went abandoned a few years back when there was a terrible storm with destructive winds and days of nonstop rain that overflowed the river and flooded the camp, destroying it. The camp was already losing money before the storm so it never rebuilt (and never will as decided by Paulwall officials). A variety of camps met here. Boy scouts, church camps, and other youth activities. Most of the cabins are gone but this one was on high enough ground the flood never got to it but it is hidden in overgrowth and tangled brush. Though the water never got inside, you can see the scummy water line in the foundation. This broken home is far enough away from the road and the path is grassed over so nobody knows of it. It looks like a craftsman house, well, more like a cottage, no a shack is more like it. Be careful when wandering abandoned properties. You never know what you'd find along the way. I will garantee a surprise is waiting in what's left of the kitchen. A squatter? The bunks are still there. Board-ups galore! No bathrooms are in the bunk house, all bathrooms were in a seperate building. This 100 year old bunk house has living room, dining room, kitchen and 2 bunk rooms. Thanks to Google for blender and other guy for propane tank. Enjoy, be careful, and please rate :)
